newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end weaker, earnings concerns dominate.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end weaker, earnings concerns dominate.

text.p: * New Zealand share market ignores RBNZ easing, ends soft
* Leaders weaken, selective buying in other issues
* Flat-to-lower earnings preoccupy investors
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
320 -5 * NZSC cap index +4.24 at 5,069.95
349 -7 * Volume NZ$55.2 million. Futures -6 at 1,120
638 -8 * Other movers - +9 +10
An easing of New Zealand monetary conditions failed to assuage investor concerns about corporate earnings, with the sharemarket ending Thursday's session on a weak note.

The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 14.50 points down at 2,251.00 on turnover worth NZ$55.2 million, despite the sharply lower interest and exchange rates resulting from the morning move by the Reserve Bank.
The bank, in its six-monthly economic forecasts, said conditions had become "inappropriately firm" and that it wanted them to ease back to where they were in December.
"I would have thought the market would have regarded it more favourably, but it hasn't so far," said Peter Lynds at ANZ Securities.
Telecom was the main culprit, dropping eight cents to NZ$6.38, but Lion Nathan was also affected, falling seven to NZ$3.49. The other leaders posted more modest falls.

"Was there enough of an easing to entice people back into the market place? People probably just thought it's going back to December levels, so the market is still really driven by earnings and the most recent results have been flat to poor," Nigel Scott at BZW said.
"People want confirmation of corporate profitabily before they look at it again," he said.
Scott said the market had become a little two-tiered in nature, with the leaders still under pressure.
But bucking the trend was Air New Zealand, the port companies and Fletcher Building.
Scott said it appeared there was some portfolio switching into defensive or recovery-style stocks.
But he said it also seemed there was some unfinished business overhanging the market.
